candidate_mechanisms.why: Large spread cells containing clusters of many small irregular DNA spots/micronuclei, low solidity/form-factor, high multinucleate and large-nucleus fractions, low cell count and frequent bright rounded cells suggest failed cytokinesis/mitotic defect typical of Aurora inhibition.

notable_cells.why: Large spread cell with ~20 punctate small blue DNA spots in shared green cytoplasm, example of multinucleate/micronucleate phenotype.
Spread cell with two grape-like clusters of small nuclei, illustrates lobed irregular multinucleate morphology.
Cell with dense cluster of small nuclei adjacent to bright yellow-white rounded cell, example of micronucleation plus mitotic-like rounding.

observations.finding: Nuclei are irregular, lobed and often as multiple discrete small bright spots within one cytoplasm vs single smooth oval nuclei in DMSO; agrees with nuc_form_factor z -45 to -46, nuc_solidity z -36 to -48, frac_multinucleate_proxy z ~16.3-16.6 value ~0.62 vs 0.268.
Increased large nuclear areas / large nuclei; agrees with frac_large_nucleus z 17.6-19.3 value ~0.08-0.09 vs 0.013.
Fields sparse with large black gaps vs near-confluent DMSO monolayer; far fewer cells per field; agrees with cell_count z -12 to -12.4 value ~83-90 vs 311.5.

Actin brighter on average and patchy/variable with strong cortical/peripheral signal and very bright rounded cells; agrees with act_mean z 9.9-14.1 and act_std z 13.6-25.1 and act_tub_ratio z 10.7-12.1.
Interphase microtubule fibrillar network less distinct/more diffuse than DMSO feathery microtubules; tubulin relatively dimmer than actin; consistent with increased act_tub_ratio z 10.7-12.1.

Numerous small bright yellow-white rounded double-positive cells consistent with mitotic arrest scattered in treated fields, rare in DMSO; no mitotic-index measurement provided so not covered by measurements.

report.uncertainty: Cannot resolve exact ploidy or distinguish Aurora vs other cytokinesis-failure/mitotic mechanisms from morphology alone; diffuse vs bundled tubulin assessment limited by contrast and cell rounding.

reflection.text:
The call was correct because quantitative atlas matching outweighed visual impression. Wells at 1 uM, 10 uM, 0.3 uM and 1 uM replicate all showed extreme irregular nuclei with nuc_form_factor z -26 to -50, nuc_solidity z -36 to -56 and frac_large_nucleus z +19 to +23, and compare_to_reference_atlas was unanimous Microtubule destabilizers 2/2 then 4/4 with 9/10 k-neighbours at 0.905-0.919 similarity.

The main misleading signal was describe_phenotype suggesting Aurora kinase inhibitors from 4 fields, which kept Aurora at 0.18 then 0.07 despite contrary atlas votes. Post-unblinding lookup did not rescue this because ChEMBL had no curated mechanisms and literature searches returned only peripheral microtubule-actin papers and zero hits for direct colcemid mechanism reviews.

The decisive acquisition choice was testing a neighboring lower dose and a replicate rather than more high doses, proving onset at 0.3 uM and reproducibility at 1 uM and justifying raising Microtubule destabilizers from 0.72 to 0.90.
what_was_right: Recognized extreme negative nuc_form_factor and nuc_solidity plus high frac_large_nucleus across e2, e3, e7, e8 as reproducible mitotic-failure signature
Trusted unanimous NSC vote in e4 and e9 with 9/10 k-neighbours and 0.905-0.919 similarity over single microscopist Aurora call in e5
Sampled 1 uM, then 10 uM, then 0.3 uM plus 1 uM replicate to demonstrate dose-consistent onset and reproducibility before submitting at p=0.90
what_was_wrong: describe_phenotype e5 candidate Aurora kinase inhibitors inflated alternative hypothesis to 0.18 and was not discriminated visually at the time
lookup_compound e12 gave no curated ChEMBL mechanisms and search_literature e13-e15 gave only peripheral papers or zero hits, so no independent literature confirmation was obtained

Retained Eg5 inhibitors and Microtubule stabilizers at low probability from 1/10 neighbour and shared cytoskeletal features without a direct discriminating measurement like spindle morphology or tubulin polymer assay
